title: Influence of polygenic risk scores on CanRisk-based risk calculation for breast and ovarian cancer in healthy relatives of non-informatively tested index individuals
summary:
A pathogenic germline variant (pV) is found in one of the currently known high or moderate risk genes (e.g. BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, CHEK2 or PALB2) in approx. 30% of all families that fulfill the inclusion criteria of the German Familial Breast and Ovarian Cancer Consortium (DK-FBREK). Conversely, in approx. 70% of families there is no pV in the risk genes examined; the genetic finding of the familial key person (index) is therefore described as “non-informative”, as a previously unknown hereditary cause cannot be ruled out. 
In the case of a non-informative genetic finding in the family, a risk calculation for a woman between the ages of 30 and 45 who does not have the disease is the basis for the offer to participate in intensified breast cancer screening.
The addition of a genetic score, calculated from individual genetic low risk variants (polygenic risk score, PRS) can optimize risk calculation for each individual. At this moment, this PRS (polygenic risk score) is not analyzed in routine care for healthy relatives of non-informatively tested index persons. Accordingly, this additional diagnostic information is currently not available to these women as input for risk calculation.     
The aim of the PRS-CHANCE study is to investigate whether the collection of the PRS in the CanRisk risk calculation influences the recommendation for intensified breast cancer screening. This will be investigated in 800 participants in this study. Determining the PRS can save women with a lower personal risk of developing breast cancer from unnecessary and too frequent examinations; women with an increased PRS risk can be included in intensified breast cancer screening.

interventions.name: Survey of the PRS (polygenic risk score) of relatives of non-informatively tested index individuals

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Families fulfill the inclusion criteria of the DK-FBREK (see DKG checklist)
- Index person is non-informative tested by gene panel analysis.
- The person seeking advice has no personal history of breast or ovarian cancer
- No other acute, palliative or prognosis-relevant (oncological) disease in personal medical history
- First to second degree of kinship (relationship coefficient R ≥ 1/4) to a family member with breast or ovarian cancer
- Age between 30 and 50 years (in this age range, inclusion in intensified breast cancer screening is possible in accordance with special care under Section 140a SGB 5)
- A possible 2nd genetic line has been excluded or clarified with an index test by gene panel analysis, which resulted in a non-informative genetic finding
- Consent to HerediCaRe and to the genetic analysis has been given or will be given as part of the study inclusion
Exclusion criteria:
- not fulfilling the above inclusion criteria
- lack of capacity to consent
- lack of consent
- Condition after bilateral mastectomy
